title: UK Economic Change: Case Studies 🏙️

walkthroughs.body_html:
The Docklands closed in the 1970s after container shipping moved away.

The LDDC (1981-1998) transformed it:
• Built Canary Wharf
• Created DLR light rail
• Attracted banks like HSBC, Barclays

Now hosts 120,000+ jobs.

To narrow the north-south divide:

• Northern Powerhouse — boost Manchester, Leeds, Liverpool
• HS2 rail — London to Birmingham (Phase 1)
• Investment in universities and skills

Critics: still London-focused spending.

hosts the UK's biggest tech cluster:

• Science Park (1970, oldest UK)
• ARM (chips), AstraZeneca (pharma)
• Strong university links

Known as 'Silicon Fen'.

mcqs.q: What is the enhanced greenhouse effect?
options: It is the hole in the ozone layer letting in more sun.
Sea level rises because of underwater volcanoes pushing it up.
The greenhouse effect is entirely man-made and harmful.
The strengthening of the natural greenhouse effect by human activities (mainly burning fossil fuels) which add CO2 and other gases to the atmosphere.

mcqs.q: What causes global sea level rise?
options: It is the hole in the ozone layer letting in more sun.
Sea level rises mainly because Arctic sea ice is melting.
Two main factors: thermal expansion of warming seawater, and the melting of land-based ice (glaciers and ice sheets) adding water to oceans.
Sea level rises because of underwater volcanoes pushing it up.

mcqs.q: Why can a cold winter NOT disprove climate change?
options: Climate is the long-term statistical average; a single cold winter is a weather event. Climate change is the trend in averages and extremes over decades, not the absence of cold days.
A really cold winter proves global warming is not happening.
It is the hole in the ozone layer letting in more sun.
Climate change only happens in summer.
